newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans ends mostly up on better mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans ends mostly up on better mood.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on speculative buying with sentiment improved after a rebound on Wednesday, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,345 yuan ($403) per tonne, rising five yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,330 yuan and hit a high of 3,348 yuan.
March did not trade, May rose 90 to 3,330 yuan, July 56 to 3,371, November unchanged at 3,350 and the January 1998 contract unchanged at 3,360.
Combined volume rose to 29,200 tonnes from 24,700.
Soybeans opened higher and rose steadily for most of the session.
Traders said many investors believed soybeans had upward potential after a rebound on Wednesday.

"More speculators are building their long positions on the market today, pushing most contracts up," one trader said. "But trading volume did not increase very much, indicating most institutions are staying on the sidelines."
Analysts said they expected soybeans to rise steadily in the next few days.
